questions.prompt: Which choice correctly contracts the words we will?

questions.prompt: Two brothers-in-law each have a workbench. Which phrase correctly refers to both men's workbenches?

Which word correctly completes the sentence?

questions.prompt:
Which form correctly completes the sentence?

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt: The writer wants to reorganize sentences 2–7 by feature: first construction, then opening behavior, then production. Which order of sentence pairs accomplishes that goal?
questions.explanation: Sentences 2 and 5 explain joining pages, 3 and 7 address opening, and 4 and 6 discuss production.
questions.stimulusTitle: Two Ways to Bind a Notebook
questions.stimulusText: (1) A notebook can be bound with thread or with adhesive. (2) Thread binding joins folded groups of pages with stitches. (3) This construction can allow the notebook to lie relatively flat when open. (4) It often involves more assembly steps and can take longer to produce. (5) Adhesive binding joins a stack of pages by gluing their prepared edges into the cover. (6) This method can be efficient when many notebooks must be produced. (7) Some adhesive-bound notebooks resist lying flat, although opening behavior varies with their materials and construction. (8) A buyer choosing between the methods should consider how the notebook will be used rather than assuming that one method is best for every purpose.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines the information in sentences 2 and 5 while emphasizing the difference between the methods?

choices.A: Thread binding stitches folded page groups together, whereas adhesive binding glues prepared page edges into the cover.
choices.B: Both methods stitch folded page groups together before gluing the same stitches into the cover.
choices.C: Adhesive binding stitches folded page groups, whereas thread binding glues their edges into the cover.
choices.D: Thread binding and adhesive binding are two names for a process whose construction is identical.

questions.correctAnswer: Thread binding stitches folded page groups together, whereas adhesive binding glues prepared page edges into the cover.
questions.explanation: Whereas presents the contrast while retaining which method uses stitches and which uses glue, without reversing or merging the processes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly capitalizes the name of a historical era?

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Precede means come before, fitting the introduction; proceed means move on or continue, fitting the transition to questions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a colon to introduce an explanation of the complete statement before it?

choices.B: The casting had one serious flaw, a crack ran through its base.

questions.explanation: Adverse means unfavorable, describing the weather; averse means opposed or unwilling, describing the crew's attitude toward postponement.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: Discreet describes tactful or unobtrusive behavior, while discrete means distinct or separate; the inquiry and the sections require those different meanings.

questions.prompt: A report compares a tunnel and a viaduct, in that order. In a later sentence, the former refers to ____ and the latter refers to ____.
questions.explanation: Former points to the first of two previously mentioned things, while latter points to the second, preserving the report's stated order.

questions.prompt: Which additional example after sentence 4 would best extend the principle that a description depends on the image's purpose?

choices.A: A cookbook and a chef's profile should use identical descriptions whenever their pages contain the same photograph.
choices.B: A photograph with more visible objects always needs a longer description, whatever topic the surrounding text discusses.
choices.C: A cookbook might describe how dough is folded, while a chef's profile might identify the person in the same photograph.
choices.D: Descriptions should list distant background objects before explaining anything connected with the article's topic.

questions.correctAnswer: A cookbook might describe how dough is folded, while a chef's profile might identify the person in the same photograph.
questions.explanation: The new example applies the same-image, different-purpose principle to another subject; the other choices ignore purpose or prescribe irrelevant priorities.
questions.stimulusText: (1) A description accompanying an image should communicate the information that readers need from that image. (2) The same photograph may need different wording in different settings. (3) In an article about stoneworking techniques, an image of a mason holding a chisel should help readers understand the tool's position and action. (4) In a biographical profile, the same image might instead identify the mason and the place of work. (5) Descriptions should not automatically list every visible detail, such as shoelaces or distant clouds. (6) If a caption already gives an important fact, the description should add what the image contributes rather than merely repeat that fact. (7) The guiding question is what purpose that particular image serves for its readers.

questions.prompt: An article explains chisel placement. Its caption already says "Mason Lea Ortiz at work." The photograph shows a chisel resting on the stone's upper edge, a raised hammer, and clouds in the distance. Which description best applies sentences 3, 5, and 6?

choices.D: Lea Ortiz is the finest stoneworker in the entire region.

questions.correctAnswer: The chisel rests on the stone's upper edge, with the mason holding the hammer above it.
questions.explanation: The correct description adds visible tool placement relevant to the article; the alternatives repeat the caption, emphasize background, or make an unsupported judgment.

choices.D: The diagram is ready, your Honor.

questions.prompt: A reviewer uses the exact phrase a quiet farewell within a larger sentence, not as a complete quoted statement or a title. Which capitalization is correct?

choices.B: The reviewer called the final movement "A Quiet Farewell."
choices.C: The reviewer called the Final Movement "a quiet farewell."
choices.D: The reviewer called the final movement "a quiet farewell."

questions.prompt: Which spelling correctly names a fine ceramic material?
questions.explanation: Porcelain ends with the letter sequence l-a-i-n; the alternatives omit the a, add an n, or replace the final letters.

questions.explanation: The replacement verb uses the ending sede; substituting cede or ceed follows a tempting but incorrect spelling pattern.

questions.prompt:
Which pair correctly completes the sentence?
The instructions were ____, and the readers became ____.
questions.explanation: Confusing describes what causes confusion; confused describes the people experiencing it, so the participial adjectives require different endings.

questions.prompt: Each diver checked the other diver's clip. Which sentence preserves that mutual meaning with the correct possessive pronoun phrase?

choices.A: The divers checked their own clips.
choices.B: The divers checked each other's clips.
choices.C: The divers checked each others' clips.
choices.D: The divers checked each other clips.

questions.correctAnswer: The divers checked each other's clips.
questions.explanation: Each other expresses the reciprocal action, and its possessive form is each other's; their own would change the action to checking personal equipment.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: A future-time clause introduced by when normally uses the present tense; the main clause's will begin already locates the event in the future.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses flaunt or flout correctly?

choices.A: The visitor was warned not to flout the rules.
choices.B: She flouted her new bracelet for everyone to admire.
choices.C: He flaunted the ban by entering a closed area.
choices.D: The tailor flouted the vibrant fabric in the display window.

questions.correctAnswer: The visitor was warned not to flout the rules.
questions.explanation: Flout means openly disregard a rule, while flaunt means display something conspicuously; the other sentences exchange those meanings.

questions.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?
The counselor asks open questions to ____ responses from quiet participants.
questions.explanation: Elicit means draw out a response; illicit means unlawful, emit means send out, and omit means leave out, none matching the counselor's purpose.

questions.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?
The narrow table stands directly ____ the armchair.
questions.explanation: Beside means next to, describing the table's position; besides means in addition to, while between and through do not fit the stated arrangement.

questions.prompt: Sentences 1–2 form the first paragraph. Which topic sentence would best introduce a second paragraph containing sentences 3–7?

choices.A: Every computer display must be constructed exactly like an opening in a wall.
choices.B: A familiar name can acquire a new use through one important resemblance.
choices.C: Physical windows have appeared in many buildings of different sizes.
choices.D: The history of every word can be explained by the invention of computer screens.

questions.correctAnswer: A familiar name can acquire a new use through one important resemblance.
questions.explanation: The proposed topic introduces the transfer of a familiar name through a shared feature, preparing both the digital example and the comparison's limits.
questions.stimulusTitle: A Word with a Second View
questions.stimulusText: (1) A physical window is an opening that frames a view of part of the surroundings. (2) Its edges select what can be seen from a particular position. (3) A computer window is a bounded region of a screen containing a document or a program's contents. (4) The display outside that region may contain other information, just as a physical window shows only part of a larger scene. (5) The shared name draws attention to a limited resemblance: both uses involve a framed view. (6) The comparison does not claim that the two things share every material or mechanism. (7) A familiar word can thus help a reader understand something new while leaving important differences intact.

questions.prompt: A writer proposes adding: "Every physical feature of the original kind must also exist in the newer kind." How should this proposal be handled?

choices.A: Omit it because it turns a limited resemblance into an unsupported claim about all features.
choices.B: Put it before sentence 1 as a definition of every possible opening.
choices.C: Put it after sentence 4 as proof that screen regions must contain glass.
choices.D: Put it after sentence 7 as a conclusion that eliminates all differences.

questions.correctAnswer: Omit it because it turns a limited resemblance into an unsupported claim about all features.
questions.explanation: The passage bases the borrowed name on a framed view while preserving other differences; the proposed sentence wrongly extends the resemblance to every feature.
